From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@finserv.com>

Subject: Vendor DPA & SCCs — Redwood Inference

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked us to get the vendor DPA and SCCs completed before we can progress to a pilot. Attached is our standard DPA with a few redlines (see clause highlights on page 3). Main asks: stronger audit rights (up to once per year for regulated data), explicit subprocessors list and 30-day notice for changes, and a carve-out on data deletion timeline for legal holds.

Could you confirm Redwood’s baseline on these items and share a plan/timeline for signature? We need execution before our internal security gating meeting on Sept 22.

Best,
Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Procurement, FinServCo
attachments: FinServ_DPA_v1_redline.docx

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-09-10 10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor DPA & SCCs — Redwood Inference

Hi Emma — appreciate the quick turnaround and the redlines.

We’ll review with Legal and security and come back with a consolidated response by EOD Monday (Sep 13). High level: Redwood accepts SCCs for EU transfers, standard subprocessors disclosure is OK but we generally provide a 10-business-day notice for additions and publish a public subprocessor list. For audit requests, we typically provide SOC 2 report and allow scoped on-site/SaaS platform reviews under NDA rather than annual full-attestation audits; we can discuss a documented procedure that meets FinServ’s controls.

Looping in Monica (solutions engineering) to confirm technical controls and Laura from Legal for contracting.

Thanks — Rishi

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai; vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai; monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-11 08:22 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Vendor DPA & SCCs — FinServCo (action: redline review)

Team — forwarding FinServ’s DPA redline. Key risk items called out by procurement: annual audit right, 30-day notice on subprocessors, and deletion timeline carve-outs. They flagged regulated data and want to ensure SCCs are attached for EU flows.

Ask: Laura — can Legal take a position on the annual audit vs SOC2 + evidence approach? Vivek — do we have a standard template response for audit scope and evidence sharing? Monica — confirm whether we can commit to 10-business-day subprocessor notice and what the retention/deletion workflow looks like (especially for legal hold).

Goal: firm position + counter-redline by Monday EOD so procurement has time for internal review.

-Rishi

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai; monica_patel@redwood.ai; vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finserv.com>
Date: 2026-09-12 11:09 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Vendor DPA & SCCs — FinServCo (counterproposal attached)

Rishi / team —

Attached is Legal’s counter-redline (Redwood_Master_DPA_2026-09-01.pdf). Summary of positions:
- Audit: we will provide SOC 2 Type II report and an option for an annual, narrowly scoped assurance review under mutual NDA. Full customer-initiated on-site audits are restricted to high-risk regulated deployments and require commercial terms.
- Subprocessors: we accept a 10-business-day advance notice and will provide an up-to-date public subprocessor page; we will supply a snapshot via shared Drive on request.
- Deletion & legal holds: we can commit to data deletion within 60 days for standard contracts; for legal holds we will preserve data and provide notice timelines.
- SCCs: confirm acceptance; attach SCCs_declaration_FIN-2026.pdf for their legal team.

Marcus (FinServ legal) — happy to take teleconf if you want to walk through the redlines. Rishi — I suggest we propose an execution plan: 1) counter-redline today, 2) 48-hour review cycle for FinServ legal, 3) route to Redwood VP Legal (Vivek) for exec signoff, 4) DocuSign circulation. That should meet their gating schedule if they review quickly.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Master_DPA_2026-09-01.pdf, SCCs_declaration_FIN-2026.pdf

From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finserv.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai; rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai; monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-13 09:48 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Vendor DPA & SCCs — FinServCo (counterproposal attached)

Laura — thanks for the detailed counter. A couple of clarifying notes from our side: the 60-day deletion window is aggressive given our record retention needs; would Redwood accept a 90-day standard deletion window with documented exceptions for legal hold? On audits — our security team would prefer a standing annual right to a scoped remote assessment that includes configuration review and sample logs. If you can include a playbook for remote evidence delivery (SAS tokens or secure upload) it would close the loop.

We can do a quick 30-minute call tomorrow morning to align and then proceed to signature.

Regards,
Marcus Lee
FinServCo — Legal Ops

Hi Emma/Marcus — thanks for the quick review and helpful feedback. Based on the call this afternoon (summary below), here’s the proposed path to signature:

1) Redwood will revert with a final DPA PDF with two amendments: 90-day deletion default, and an explicit procedure for remote scoped assessments (SOC 2 + sample evidence upload via secure Drive link).
2) FinServ legal to confirm acceptance within 48 hours.
3) Upon acceptance, we’ll route the final PDF to Vivek (VP Legal) for exec approval and then to DocuSign for signatures — I’ll coordinate the envelope and notify procurement.

Attachments: final DPA will include SCCs_declaration_FIN-2026.pdf.

Timing note: if FinServ confirms by Sept 16 EOD, we can have signed DPA in DocuSign by Sept 19, which meets your gating meeting on Sept 22.

Next steps for Redwood: Laura to issue final PDF by EOD tomorrow; Monica to prepare brief technical evidence pack (SOC 2 excerpt, control matrix) for secure upload. Vivek — please expect a request for exec signature on Friday.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if anything changes.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
